title: Spreading an injective generic product map and coordinate idempotents
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian domain, $B$ a finite commutative $A$-algebra [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft], $K$ a fraction field of $A$, and $K'$ a field extension of $K$ [def-pc-field-extension] with a compatible $A$-algebra structure. Let $r$ be a natural number and $L_j$ fields over $K'$ for $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$. Suppose the reduction of $(K\otimes_A B)\otimes_K K'$ is isomorphic as a $K'$-algebra to $\prod_j L_j$. Fix $0
e c_0\in A$, a subalgebra $S_0\subset K'$ that is the localization $A[1/c_0]$, and a subalgebra $A_0\subset K'$ over $S_0$, finite etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], with fraction field $K'$ and surjective spectrum map [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then there exist $0
e c\in A$ and a domain $A'$ in the universe of $A$, with compatible $A[1/c]$- and $A$-algebra structures, finite etale with surjective spectrum map over $A[1/c]$, and an $A'$-algebra structure on $K'$ making it a fraction field of $A'$. There are $A'$-algebra structures on the $L_j$ with towers $A'	o K'	o L_j$, and an injective $A'$-algebra map $f:(B\otimes_A A')_{\mathrm{red}}	o\prod_j L_j$. For every $j$ there is $e_j$ in its source such that $f(e_j)_i=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. For every $j$ and $z\in L_j$ there are $0
e a\in A'$ and $x$ in the source with $a z=f(x)_j$. No domain factors or product equivalence are asserted.

proof.text: Form C = (B tensor A0)_red. Tensor associativity and the equality of the localized nilradical with the nilradical of the localization identify its generic fibre with the specified product of fields. The kernel of the map from C to this generic fibre is torsion. Since A0 is finite over the Noetherian localization S0, both A0 and the finite A0-module C are Noetherian. Finitely many generators of the kernel have nonzero annihilators; invert their product to make the map injective.

The coordinate idempotents have numerators in C and nonzero denominators in A0. Invert the product of these finitely many denominators. Their numerators divided by their denominators then give the elements e_j with the stated images. Surjectivity of the generic map expresses each field element in each coordinate as a numerator over a nonzero base denominator, which gives the last identity. When r = 0 the generic ring is zero and torsion killing kills all of C; the coordinate assertions are vacuous.

For every nonzero element t of A0 to be inverted, choose a monic integral equation over S0 of smallest degree. Its constant coefficient is nonzero: if it vanished, cancel t in the domain to obtain a lower-degree monic equation. That constant coefficient belongs to the principal ideal generated by t. Clearing the coefficients c0 denominators gives a nonzero element of A whose invertibility makes t invertible. Localize A at the product of these elements and c0. The base change of A0 is a localization of the domain A0, hence a domain with fraction field K prime; it is finite etale and surjective by base change. The tensor quotient and embedding above identify with those over this model.

The localized model is finite over A[1/c], a ring in the universe of A, hence admits a small finite-module presentation. Transport the ring, algebra, fraction-ring and spectrum properties and embedding along this presentation to put A prime in the universe of A. Give each L_j its A prime algebra structure by composing through K prime. These maps give the scalar towers and transport the idempotent and denominator identities.
